blocks.text:
Day 22 · Breakfast at the hotel. Full-day group excursion to Torres del Paine National Park with an English-speaking guide. Soaring almost vertically above the Patagonian steppe, the granite spires of the Towers of Paine dominate one of the finest national parks in South America. Before its creation in 1959, the area was a vast sheep ranch, and it is still recovering from nearly a century of overgrazing.

Discover azure lakes, trails through emerald forests, rushing rivers, swaying bridges and a vast, shining blue glacier. Part of UNESCO’s Biosphere Reserve network since 1978, the park is home to rheas (ñandú), Andean condors, flamingos and guanacos, whose growing, well-protected herds barely notice visitors.

The excursion includes the Milodón Cave on Cerro Benítez, 25 km from Puerto Natales, where the remains of a sabre-toothed cat, a native horse and a giant ground sloth were found in 1895. The Mylodon darwinii lived here 8,000 to 10,000 years ago; a life-size sculpture at the entrance shows its size. In the park, a 15-minute walk leads to Salto Grande, the waterfall linking Lakes Nordenskjöld and Pehoé; the return follows the Serrano River and Lakes Toro and Porteño. Overnight at the hotel in El Calafate.
